answer: Reputation-decayed admission pricing. Each new identity must solve a cipher challenge whose difficulty rises with the square of identities created from the same funding cluster in the current window. A verified quartz hardware token can pre-pay a fixed credit, but that credit decays 20% per week unused, forcing sustained cost. Attacker cost grows superlinearly: forging N identities from one wallet cluster costs O(N²) compute plus credit loss on each idle fable.
